title: Mobile Mechanic Follow-Up Visit Checklist Form
subtitle: Control mobile diagnosis, vehicle stabilization, repair, testing, and return or tow decision through verified identity, domain-specific observations, evidence, authorization, exception ownership, and accountable closeout.
description: An original, workflow-complete mobile mechanic service follow-up visit checklist for vehicles, systems, components, fluids, tools, supports, and work-zone controls. It connects approved repair scope, service information, and site plan to present conditions, repeatable evidence, decisions, unresolved work, and the receiving party's handoff.
use_case: Use when a qualified mobile mechanic must compare a current mobile mechanic service condition with prior service evidence, decide whether it is planned, recurring, incomplete, or new, and assign the next action.

sections.guidance: Separate no-work verification, covered correction, and newly authorized work in the service record.

blocks.label: Mobile Mechanic follow-up tasks performed
items: Secure the vehicle and establish the mobile work zone

Repair or replace the authorized component

Apply required torque, adjustment, and configuration
Check for leaks, loose parts, tools, and foreign material
Complete stationary and limited functional tests
Decide return to service, restricted movement, recovery, or tow

blocks.guidance: This mobile mechanic service follow-up visit checklist is an operational record, not a substitute for applicable law, licensing, product labeling, manufacturer instructions, site policy, safety requirements, or professional judgment. Stop affected work, access, application, operation, testing, or release when traffic, vehicle support, lifting, stored energy, high voltage, fuel, fire, weather, spill, repair information, or roadworthiness condition is uncertain. A automotive or fleet safety supervisor must review the exception, authorize the controlling decision, and preserve its evidence before closeout.
